title: How Far a Voucher Stands from Lapsing, and What That Releases on the Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
A voucher on an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking that is still a long way from lapsing releases more of its standing value at one movement than one close to its expiry. Two readings decide it: how far the voucher's expiry stands from today, and whether the fare brand that produced it makes its credits transferable.

## 1. The release share

| Where | The share released is |
| --- | --- |
| the voucher standing on the booking lapses more than 6 months from today and the fare brand makes its credits transferable | 1, the whole of the standing value |
| the voucher standing on the booking lapses more than 6 months from today and the brand does not make its credits transferable | 0.98, being 98 percent |
| in every other case | no such treatment applies to the release share |

The lapse test is measured in months from today to the expiry recorded on the most recent voucher standing on the booking, and must exceed 6: a voucher lapsing in exactly 6 months does not exceed it. The transferability test reads the term scheduled for the brand the booking is held in.

## 2. Input, judgement and outcome, on hypothetical figures

**Input.** A voucher standing on a Premium Economy Select booking, expiring 11 months from today.
**Judgement.** 11 months exceeds 6, and the brand makes its credits transferable.
**Outcome.** The whole of the standing value is released at one movement.

**Input.** A voucher standing on an Economy Classic booking, expiring 11 months from today.
**Judgement.** 11 months exceeds 6, but the brand does not make its credits transferable.
**Outcome.** 98 percent of the standing value is released.

**Input.** A voucher standing on a Business Flex booking, expiring 5 months from today.
**Judgement.** 5 months does not exceed 6, so neither of the first two rows holds however the brand treats transferability.
**Outcome.** No such treatment applies to the release share.
